scope: Interrupted native QEMU workload prefix, not H10 completion. All original process identities are missing; a reused PID belongs to a different full-test child. Windows has not rebooted since launch. Cause of process termination is unknown.

analysis.scope:
Audit a native runtime journal and compare free heap in equal workload phases.

This reads files only and never connects to or pauses the guest. A diagnostic
prefix of an active workload is explicitly pending, never a completed H10 pass.

limitations: Observed phase/window medians and variation do not prove absence of every possible leak.
SDK minimum is cumulative; a constant minimum can coexist with declining current free heap.
Retained changes require an explanation or a firmware fix before accepting the soak.
This audits native QEMU runtime only; it does not establish physical-board acceptance.
The workload uses a fixed NTP epoch; this is not a continuous calendar/DST test.
Task stack fill and sampled free heap cannot prove every interrupt or transient allocation peak.
Retained memory loss is a finding to investigate, not automatically an allowed SDK cache.

stale_supervisor.scope: Child process supervision only; not a 24-hour or memory-trend acceptance.

nonterminal_guard.scope: Independent UART boot/panic guard; not a memory trend or 24-hour pass.
